patients.summary: Healthy environmental field technician who joined in 2023 and was diagnosed with acute lymphoblastic leukemia after a practice CBC in fall 2025. Induction was complicated by febrile neutropenia, maintenance by Pseudomonas bacteremia with ecthyma gangrenosum, and in June 2026 he had Rocky Mountain spotted fever after a hiking trip; oncology runs his leukemia care.

documents.title: New Patient Call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is a 26 y/o man who moved to the hilltowns for work last year and has not had a regular doctor since college. Wants to get established. Has commercial PPO through employer, card info taken. Scheduled new patient visit 9/19 at 8:00 am, first appointment of the day per his request (he is out in the field most days). Asked him to fill out the health history form in the portal before he comes.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
26 y/o M establishing care. Last physical was through student health several years ago. No complaints today.

PMH: seasonal allergies since his teens, worst in spring and again in late August. Gets by with avoiding mowing and showering after field days; does not take anything regularly.
PSH: T&A at age 7.
Meds: none.
Allergies: Bactrim-type antibiotic (sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim) as a kid, his mother told him his throat swelled and he needed epinephrine, so he treats it as anaphylaxis. IV contrast for a CT years ago gave him hives, he does not remember details.
FH: father with high blood pressure, mother on thyroid replacement for hypothyroidism, paternal grandfather had AML in his mid-60s.
SH: environmental field technician for a consulting firm, does soil and water sampling, a lot of time in brush and wetlands. Never smoked. 2-3 beers a week. No other substances. Single, lives alone, hikes and fishes on weekends.

ROS negative except as above.

Exam: well-appearing, vitals as charted. HEENT normal, TMs clear, mild pale nasal turbinates. Neck supple without adenopathy or thyromegaly. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no organomegaly. Skin without rashes. Normal gait and affect.

A/P:
1. Health maintenance: CBC, CMP, lipids, one-time HIV and hep C screening today. Flu and COVID shots in October, will come in for a nurse visit. Tdap due next year by his recollection of his last one.
2. Seasonal allergic rhinitis, mild: nonpharmacologic measures are working for him. Revisit if symptoms escalate.
3. Allergies reviewed and entered. Discussed tick checks given his job.
RTC one year.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Calvin, your blood counts, kidney and liver tests, and cholesterol all came back normal. HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative, and those don't need repeating unless something changes. Nice to meet you this week.

documents.title: Immunization Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here before work for seasonal flu and the 2023-24 COVID booster. Afebrile, feels well. No egg or vaccine reactions in the past. Flu vaccine L deltoid, COVID R deltoid, lot numbers in the MAR. Waited 15 min in the lobby without issue. VIS sheets given.

documents.title: Vaccine record for work
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, my company is updating its field safety files and wants a copy of my vaccine history. Can you send what you have? Thanks, Calvin

documents.title: RE: Vaccine record for work
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Hi Calvin, I uploaded your immunization record to the documents section of the portal. It has what we gave in October plus what you reported at your first visit. Let us know if your employer needs a signed form.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
27M for yearly exam. Busy summer of fieldwork, feels fine. Allergy season was tolerable. No new meds.

Exam: vitals reviewed, BP normal. Pleasant, fit. Oropharynx clear. No lymphadenopathy. RRR, lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no hepatosplenomegaly. Skin: no rashes, no suspicious nevi. Neuro grossly normal.

Assessment/plan:
- Routine adult exam. CBC and CMP drawn. Lipids fine last year, skip this round.
- Tdap given today, his last one could not be confirmed.
- Allergic rhinitis, seasonal, stable without medication.
- Flu shot and updated COVID vaccine at a nurse visit in late October once supply is in.
- Tick bite prevention reviewed: permethrin-treated work clothes, repellent, daily checks.
See in a year.

documents.title: Annual labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: CBC and metabolic panel normal. Released to portal with a short note.

documents.title: Immunization Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Seasonal influenza and 2024-25 COVID vaccine given, one in each arm. Tolerated well last year with only a sore arm. Observed 15 minutes, no reaction. Pt asked about Lyme vaccine for work; told him none is on the market for adults right now and to keep up with permethrin and tick checks.

documents.title: Cancellation
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt called to cancel his 8/12 physical. Out on a multi-week sampling job through the end of the month. Will call back to rebook for the fall.

documents.title: Tired and bruising
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I never rebooked my physical but something seems off. I've been wiped out for about three weeks, way more than a long field season should do, and I keep finding bruises on my shins that I don't remember getting. Can I get in early next week?

documents.title: RE: Tired and bruising
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Calvin, thanks for writing. I've put you on the doctor's schedule Monday 9/29 at 8:30 and we will draw labs at that visit. If you have any bleeding that won't stop, black stools, fever or feel faint over the weekend, go to the ED.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 28M with roughly three weeks of fatigue out of proportion to his workload. Bruises on both shins without trauma he can recall. No fevers, sweats, nosebleeds, gum bleeding, melena or hematuria. No new medicines or supplements. No recent illness.

O: Vitals as charted, afebrile. Looks pale and tired. Conjunctival pallor. Oropharynx without petechiae. No cervical, axillary or inguinal nodes. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, liver and spleen not palpable. Skin: several 1-3 cm ecchymoses over both anterior shins at different stages, no petechiae elsewhere.

A/P: Fatigue with unexplained bruising in a previously well young man. Worried about a marrow process. CBC with diff drawn now, asked lab to call critical values and do a smear review. Will call him today with results.

documents.title: CBC and smear
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: WBC 2.4, Hgb 10.1, plt 64, ANC 0.9. Analyzer flagged the lymphocyte count; pathologist smear review shows 22% blasts. Called the on-call hematologist at the regional cancer center, who will see him Wednesday 10/1 with marrow that day. Urgent referral placed. Called patient, see phone note.

documents.title: Results call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reached pt. Explained his counts are low and there are immature cells in the blood that need a bone marrow exam, and that leukemia is on the list. He took it calmly, asked good questions, a friend will drive him Wednesday. Bleeding and fever precautions reviewed, no contact sports or heavy lifting at work this week. He knows to call or go to the ED for fever 38 or above.

documents.title: Referral faxed
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Referral, visit note, CBC and smear report faxed to the cancer center hematology intake. Confirmed receipt by phone; pt is on their schedule 10/1 at 9:00. Pt notified via portal.

documents.title: Hematology/Oncology Consultation
documents.author: hematology/oncology
documents.body:
Regional cancer center, Leukemia Service. Date of consultation 10/01/2025.

Thank you for the prompt referral of Mr. Sawyer, a 28-year-old man with three weeks of fatigue and bruising, found by you to have pancytopenia with 22% circulating blasts.

History, medications (none) and family history reviewed; of note his paternal grandfather had AML in his sixties. Allergies: sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim (anaphylaxis, by report), iodinated contrast (urticaria).

Exam today matched yours: pallor, shin ecchymoses, no adenopathy or organomegaly.

Bone marrow aspirate and biopsy were performed today. Morphology and immunophenotyping show a hypercellular marrow replaced by lymphoblasts, diagnostic of acute lymphoblastic leukemia.

Plan: right subclavian port placed by interventional radiology 10/02 without complication. Admitted 10/03 to begin induction chemotherapy on our inpatient leukemia unit. We discussed the diagnosis, treatment phases and expected length of therapy with him at length. We will keep you updated with letters at each phase.

Hematology/Oncology attending, Leukemia Service

documents.title: Consult letter reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed. ALL confirmed, inpatient induction started 10/3. Problem list updated. Sent him a note wishing him well and letting him know we're here for anything outside oncology.

conditions.label: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia not having achieved remission

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily during neutropenic periods as directed by oncology
Inject 300 mcg under the skin daily during nadir periods as directed by oncology

documents.title: Discharge Summary, Leukemia Service
documents.author: hematology/oncology
documents.body:
Admitted 10/03/2025, discharged 10/31/2025.
Principal diagnosis: acute lymphoblastic leukemia, induction chemotherapy.
Secondary: febrile neutropenia due to chemotherapy; chemotherapy-related thrombocytopenia.
Allergies: sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim (anaphylaxis by patient report; desensitized per our protocol), iodinated contrast (urticaria).

Hospital course: Induction began 10/03 through his right subclavian port. On hospital day 10 (10/12) he had rigors with a temperature of 40.1 C. He looked unwell, but a careful exam found no source: port site clean, lungs clear, no mucositis, skin intact. Labs that morning: WBC 0.38, ANC 0.02, Hgb 8.4, MCV 89, platelets 58. Blood cultures from the port and a peripheral site were sent, and IV cefepime was begun right after. Counts stayed profoundly low over the next several days, and after team discussion filgrastim was added. He defervesced on day 3 of cefepime; cultures had no growth at 5 days and cefepime was stopped after count recovery.

End-of-induction bone marrow 10/30: morphologic complete remission.

Discharge medications: valacyclovir 500 mg daily; ciprofloxacin 500 mg twice daily whenever ANC falls below 500, per written instructions; filgrastim 300 mcg subcut daily during nadir periods per written instructions.

Follow-up: outpatient leukemia clinic weekly, next cycle per protocol. Return precautions for fever 38.0 C or higher.

Leukemia Service hospitalist

documents.title: Discharge summary reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Summary reviewed. Induction complicated by culture-negative febrile neutropenia, now in remission. Lists updated with oncology's prophylaxis meds and the neutropenia and thrombocytopenia. Front desk to book a check-in next week.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here to check in after his month-long induction stay. Tired, appetite coming back slowly, down about 4 kg since September. No fevers since discharge. Sleeping OK. Getting his next chemotherapy cycle at the cancer center clinic; they draw counts there and he knows when to start cipro and filgrastim. On leave from work.

Meds reconciled: valacyclovir daily; cipro and filgrastim per oncology's nadir instructions. Allergies unchanged.

Exam: thin, alert, wearing a mask. Afebrile, vitals as charted. Port R upper chest, clean, nontender. No oral ulcers. Lungs clear, heart regular. A few fading bruises on the legs.

A/P:
1. ALL in remission after induction, on active therapy with oncology. Counts and chemotherapy decisions stay with them.
2. History of febrile neutropenia: fever plan reviewed, he goes straight to the cancer center ED, not urgent care.
3. Weight loss with treatment, encouraged calorie-dense foods.
4. Flu vaccine: will ask oncology about timing, inactivated only, no live vaccines while on treatment.
Check in again in 2 months, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Leave paperwork
documents.author: patient
documents.body: HR at my company sent a medical leave certification form. Oncology already did one but HR wants my regular doctor to sign the section about how long I'll be out. Can I drop it off?

documents.title: RE: Leave paperwork
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sure. Drop it at the front desk or upload it here. I'll fill in that I agree with oncology's estimate and refer HR to them for the specifics of your treatment schedule.

documents.title: Form completed
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Leave certification signed by PCP, copy scanned, original faxed to employer HR per pt's release.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Checking in mid-treatment. Doing the outpatient chemotherapy blocks at the cancer center, says the last one was rough for a week and then he bounced back. No fevers since fall. Weight up a little. Mood is fine, he's been reading and tying flies, misses being outside for work. PHQ-9 3.

Meds unchanged: valacyclovir daily, cipro and filgrastim only when oncology tells him.

Exam: afebrile, vitals as charted. Port site clean. Mouth without sores. Lungs clear, RRR. No edema, no bruising today.

A/P:
1. ALL in remission, intensive phase ongoing per oncology.
2. Influenza vaccine: his oncologist's nurse confirmed by phone this morning that inactivated flu vaccine is fine at this point in his cycle. Given today. Household contacts should be vaccinated too.
3. Mood screen reassuring.
See in about 3 months or after his next oncology phase.

documents.title: Leukemia Clinic Progress Letter
documents.author: hematology/oncology
documents.body:
Leukemia clinic, regional cancer center. Visit 02/04/2026.

Dear colleague, an update on our shared patient. He remains in complete remission and is tolerating his intensive treatment blocks with expected count drops, managed with his nadir plan (ciprofloxacin and filgrastim). No admissions since induction. We anticipate finishing the intensive phase in March and moving to oral maintenance.

Current medications: valacyclovir 500 mg daily; ciprofloxacin 500 mg BID and filgrastim 300 mcg daily during nadir periods.
Allergies: sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim (anaphylaxis per patient; desensitized per oncology protocol); iodinated contrast (urticaria).

Leukemia clinic attending

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets (100 mg) by mouth nightly
Take 6 tablets (15 mg) by mouth once weekly

documents.title: Leukemia Clinic Letter: Maintenance
documents.author: hematology/oncology
documents.body:
Leukemia clinic, regional cancer center. Visit 03/30/2026.

He completed his final intensive cycle on 03/20/2026 and remains in remission. Maintenance therapy began today: mercaptopurine 100 mg by mouth nightly and methotrexate 15 mg by mouth once weekly, with counts every 2 to 4 weeks here and doses adjusted to his counts. Continue valacyclovir 500 mg daily. Ciprofloxacin 500 mg BID and filgrastim 300 mcg daily remain on his nadir instructions; we expect a low count stretch over the next few weeks as he recovers from the last block.

Please avoid live vaccines. Allergies: sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim (anaphylaxis by report; desensitized per oncology protocol); iodinated contrast (urticaria).

Leukemia clinic attending

documents.title: Letter reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Maintenance started 3/30. Added 6-MP and weekly methotrexate to his list as oncology-prescribed.

conditions.label: Ecthyma gangrenosum due to Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteremia

medications.sig: 2 g IV every 8 hours through port by home infusion, last dose 4/25

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Cancer center emergency department. Seen 04/11/2026.

CC: fever, painful spots on legs.

HPI: 28-year-old man with ALL, now in maintenance, with a prior admission for chemotherapy-induced neutropenia. Two days of fever and a painful rash on both lower legs. His last chemotherapy cycle finished about three weeks ago.

Meds: mercaptopurine 100 mg nightly, methotrexate 15 mg weekly, valacyclovir 500 mg daily, ciprofloxacin 500 mg BID (taking), filgrastim 300 mcg daily per nadir plan. Allergies: sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim (anaphylaxis, by report; desensitized per oncology), iodinated contrast (urticaria).

Triage: T 38.9 C, BP 90/60, HR 120, RR 22.

Exam: ill-appearing, flushed. Port site clean. Lungs clear. Tachycardic, regular. Abdomen soft. Skin: several round red macules over both lower legs, many now with a central blister and a rim of redness; one lesion on the left calf has a black necrotic center ringed by erythema.

Labs: WBC 1.2, Hgb 9.2, platelets 50. Blood cultures x2 drawn.

MDM: febrile neutropenia with hypotension and necrotic skin lesions, concerning for ecthyma gangrenosum from gram-negative bacteremia. IV fluids, cefepime given after cultures. Admitted to the leukemia service.

Emergency medicine attending

documents.title: Discharge Summary, Leukemia Service
documents.author: hematology/oncology
documents.body:
Admitted 04/11/2026, discharged 04/21/2026.
Diagnoses: Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteremia with ecthyma gangrenosum; chemotherapy-induced neutropenia; thrombocytopenia.

Course: Both blood culture sets grew Pseudomonas aeruginosa, susceptible to cefepime. Continued cefepime 2 g IV every 8 hours. Blood pressure responded to fluids. Filgrastim given until neutrophils recovered. Fever resolved by day 4. Leg lesions treated with local wound care; the necrotic lesion is crusting with dry eschar. Plan is 14 days of cefepime total, last dose 04/25, finished at home through his port with a home infusion agency.

Discharge medications: cefepime 2 g IV q8h through 04/25; resume valacyclovir; mercaptopurine 100 mg nightly and methotrexate 15 mg weekly; ciprofloxacin and filgrastim per nadir plan.
Allergies: sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim (anaphylaxis per patient; desensitized per oncology protocol); iodinated contrast (urticaria).
Follow-up: leukemia clinic in 1 week; PCP within a few days.

Leukemia Service hospitalist

documents.title: Records reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: P. aeruginosa bacteremia with ecthyma gangrenosum, home cefepime through 4/25. Added to list. RN to call him today, visit Friday.

documents.title: Post-discharge Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt the day after discharge. Home infusion nurse came last night, line working, doses on schedule. No fever at home, legs sore but less. Changing the leg dressings himself per the wound instructions. Reviewed med list with him against the discharge summary, matches. Visit Fri 4/24 at 10:30 confirmed.

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen 3 days after discharge from a 10-day admission for P. aeruginosa bacteremia with ecthyma gangrenosum during early maintenance chemotherapy. Feels much better. No fevers at home. Last cefepime dose is tomorrow, infusion nurse following. Leukemia clinic visit next week, they will check counts.

Meds reconciled with the discharge list: cefepime through 4/25, mercaptopurine 100 mg nightly, methotrexate 15 mg weekly, valacyclovir 500 mg daily, cipro and filgrastim per nadir plan.

Exam: afebrile, vitals as charted, BP normal today. Port accessed, dressing clean and dry. Lungs clear, heart regular. Legs: healing lesions on both shins, the left calf one with a firm dry black eschar and a thin pink rim, no fluctuance, no drainage, no spreading redness. Others are flat, pink and crusted.

A/P:
1. Pseudomonas bacteremia with ecthyma gangrenosum: improving, finishing 14 days of cefepime tomorrow. Keep dressings dry; leave the eschar alone. Call for fever, new spots or redness tracking up the leg.
2. Chemotherapy-induced neutropenia: counts per oncology. Fever plan unchanged, cancer center ED.
3. ALL in remission on maintenance, oncology following.
4. Weight a bit down again, eating well now.
Follow-up later this year, sooner if needed. He will message once he's back at work.

documents.title: Back to work
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Oncology cleared me to go back to work part time on light field duty. Legs are healed except a scar on the left calf. My manager wants a note from you too, can you send one?

documents.title: RE: Back to work
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Great news. A return-to-work letter matching oncology's restrictions is in your documents tab. Keep up the tick protection out there, and remember a fever means a call to the cancer center first.

documents.title: Hospital again
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Heads up, I was in the hospital last week for two nights. Went hiking in Arkansas and came back with a fever and bad headache, they said it was probably Rocky Mountain spotted fever from the ticks and put me on doxycycline. Feeling a lot better, finishing the pills Tuesday. Just wanted you to know.

documents.title: RE: Hospital again
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for telling me, Calvin, and I'm glad you're on the mend. I'll ask the hospital for the records. Finish every dose of the doxycycline. Let's plan to see you in the fall.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Cancer center emergency department. Seen 06/23/2026.

CC: fever, headache, body aches x 6 days.

HPI: 29-year-old man with ALL in maintenance, prior admissions for febrile neutropenia during induction and for P. aeruginosa bacteremia with ecthyma gangrenosum. Six days of fever, headache and myalgias that began after he got home from a hiking trip in rural Arkansas, where he pulled several ticks off his legs. He never saw a rash. Light hurts his eyes and he is mildly nauseated. No vomiting, cough or sore throat.

Meds: mercaptopurine 100 mg nightly, methotrexate 15 mg weekly, valacyclovir 500 mg daily. Allergies: sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim (anaphylaxis per report; desensitized per oncology), iodinated contrast (urticaria).

Exam: T 38.6 C. Uncomfortable. Mild bilateral scleral injection. Tender cervical lymph nodes. Neck supple. Lungs clear, heart regular. Abdomen soft. Skin: scattered petechiae on both ankles and wrists. Port site clean.

Labs: WBC 3.1, Hgb 12.6, platelets 112; AST 92, ALT 104. Rickettsial serology sent.

MDM: febrile illness with tick exposure in an endemic area, petechiae at wrists and ankles, low platelets and transaminase rise: treating for Rocky Mountain spotted fever. Doxycycline 100 mg IV given. Admitted to medicine given immunosuppression.

Emergency medicine attending

documents.title: Discharge Summary, Medicine
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Admitted 06/23/2026, discharged 06/25/2026.
Diagnosis: Rocky Mountain spotted fever, clinical, acute serology R. rickettsii IgG 1:64; convalescent titer to be drawn in about 3 weeks at the leukemia clinic.

Course: Doxycycline 100 mg twice daily, IV first dose then oral. Afebrile within 48 hours, headache gone, petechiae fading. Oncology aware.

Discharge medications: doxycycline 100 mg by mouth twice daily to complete 7 days total (through 06/30); otherwise continue home medications.
Allergies: sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim (anaphylaxis per patient; desensitized per oncology protocol); iodinated contrast (urticaria).
Follow-up: leukemia clinic, PCP.

Hospital medicine attending

documents.title: Records filed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: June admission for presumed RMSF reviewed, doxy course ends today. Filed. Will review at his fall visit.

documents.author: hematology/oncology
documents.body:
Leukemia clinic, regional cancer center. Visit 07/14/2026.

Seen in follow-up after his June admission. Fully recovered, back at work. Convalescent Rickettsia rickettsii IgG today is 1:512 against 1:64 at presentation, a fourfold rise that confirms Rocky Mountain spotted fever. He remains in remission and continues maintenance mercaptopurine 100 mg nightly and methotrexate 15 mg weekly with valacyclovir 500 mg daily; ciprofloxacin and filgrastim per nadir plan.
Allergies: sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim (anaphylaxis by report; desensitized per oncology protocol); iodinated contrast (urticaria).

Leukemia clinic attending
